title: The Organization Practice in Context

header.html: 3.2.1 Apply the organization practice: project management team structure, role descriptions, commercial management approach, areas of focus of the key roles, effective management and techniques; 3.2.2 analyze whether an approach is effective and fit for purpose, considering the principles, the techniques and tailoring
the official PRINCE2 7 Practitioner syllabus (PeopleCert, version 7.2)

toc.title: Purpose and the principles it serves
The team and the key roles

html:
1Purpose and the principles it serves

The organization practice sets up the accountability structure of the project: who is responsible for what, who decides, who reports to whom, and how the project works with its suppliers. Every project must represent three interests: business, user and supplier.

The main principle is define roles, responsibilities and relationships. The practice also serves manage by exception (delegation within tolerances), manage by stages (the board authorizes each stage and the team is reviewed at stage ends), focus on products (work goes to teams as work packages) and tailor.

In the Official Book, products are in 6.5, roles in Table 6.4, management and techniques in 6.2 and 6.3, and tailoring in 6.7.

2The management products

All three are parts of the PID.

Product What it is for
Project management team structure Shows the roles, who holds them, and the reporting and delegation lines
Role descriptions What each role is responsible for, its authority and the skills needed; each named person agrees to theirs
Commercial management approach How the project works with suppliers: what is bought, contract and procurement arrangements, supplier performance and contract changes
Exam tip

. The structure shows who, the role descriptions show what each person does, and the commercial management approach shows how suppliers fit. All three are in the PID, not in the project log.

3The team and the key roles

Level Who Focus
Corporate or programme Senior management Mandate; appoints the executive; sets project tolerances
Directing Project board Accountable for success; authorizes stages; decides on exceptions
Managing Project manager Day-to-day management within tolerances
Delivering Team managers and team members Produce the products in work packages
Role Area of focus
Executive Single point of accountability; owns the business case; leads the board
Senior user Speaks for the users: specifies their needs and ensures the products meet them
Senior supplier Speaks for the supplier: commits supplier resources and is accountable for supplier quality
Project manager Plans, controls and reports within tolerances; manages the team managers
Team manager Delivers work packages to the agreed quality, time and cost
Project assurance Independent checks for the board on the business, user and supplier interests
Change authority Decides changes within the limits the board delegated
Project support Administration: tools, records, reports and advice

Check Table 6.4 in the book when two roles seem to fit.

Exam tip

. Project assurance must be independent of the project manager. If the project manager, or someone who reports to the project manager, assures the work, the approach is not fit for purpose.

4Effective management and techniques

  • A balanced board. The business, user and supplier interests are each represented by someone with the authority to decide, the time to attend and the right seniority. One executive. A board small enough to decide.
  • Delegation. The board delegates day-to-day management to the project manager within tolerances; the project manager delegates work to team managers through work packages; the board delegates small changes to a change authority within a limit. The board keeps its time for decisions.
  • Choosing people. Pick for authority, competence, availability and conflicts of interest. Stakeholder analysis helps. Each person agrees to their role description.
  • Communication lines. Everyone knows whom they report to; the supplier's team manager reports progress to the project manager.
  • Commercial arrangements. The contract fits the stage structure and tolerances, supplier reporting matches project reporting, and the supplier's representative can commit resources.
  • Techniques. A work breakdown structure and a responsibility matrix help allocate work and accountability.
  • Review. Revisit the team at stage boundaries, when people and needs change.
Exam tip

. The change authority decides only inside the limit the board delegated. Above that limit, or when a tolerance is affected, the decision goes back to the project board.

5Judging a scenario

Area Effective Red flag Principle
Board balance All three interests represented by people with authority Supplier absent; user voice cannot accept products Define roles
Board size and time Small board whose members attend Large committee; absent members Define roles
Accountability One executive; project manager works within tolerances Two owners; the project manager acts as executive Define roles
Delegation Routine decisions with the project manager; small changes with the change authority Board approves routine items; project manager decides a tolerance breach Manage by exception
Assurance Independent of the project manager Project manager assures own work Define roles
Commercial Contract dates and reports fit stages and tolerances Contract ignores stages; supplier staff fill board roles Manage by stages
Records Structure and role descriptions in the PID, agreed by named people Roles assumed, never written down Define roles

Tailoring:

  • Small project: roles can be combined (the project manager as team manager and support) and the board kept small, but the three interests stay represented and assurance stays independent.
  • Multi-party: several senior suppliers or users on the board, agreed spokespeople to keep it small, a team manager for each supplier and a formal commercial management approach.
  • Agile delivery: a product owner may speak for the senior user and a delivery lead may act as team manager; the team organizes its own work inside work packages; the board and project manager roles stay.
Exam tip

. Tailoring may combine roles but never removes an interest or the independence of assurance. An option that drops the supplier or the user voice from the board because the project is small is wrong.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Marta Quinn proposes removing Lena Kovac from the Project Harbor board, because Delta Software is only a contractor and the board should hold Brightwater staff alone. Was this appropriate, and why?

  • AYes, because suppliers should be managed through the contract and not sit on the board
  • BYes, because a board of Brightwater staff alone decides faster and keeps matters private
  • CNo, because the supplier interest needs a senior supplier able to commit supplier resources
  • DNo, because the senior supplier chairs the board and approves the business case for the project
Show the answer

Answer: C. Define roles, responsibilities and relationships requires the supplier interest to sit on the board through someone who can commit supplier resources, while the contract only covers commercial terms.

S2Short of staff, Sam Okafor plans to cover project assurance for the pilot stage of Project Harbor by reviewing his own plans. What should Sam do?

  • AAsk the board to arrange independent assurance, such as Aisha Bello
  • BKeep reviewing his own plans and record each review as assurance
  • CAsk Jon Park, who reports to him, to carry out the assurance checks
  • DAsk Wei Chen to assure the supplier's work and report it to him
Show the answer

Answer: A. Project assurance must be independent of the project manager, so it comes from a board-appointed person and not from Sam or people who report to him.

S3The board gave Tomas Reyes authority over changes up to 10,000 in Project Harbor. A request for a new payment feature would cost 40,000. Who should decide it?

  • ATomas Reyes, because he holds the change authority role
  • BSam Okafor, because he manages the budget for changes
  • CLena Kovac, because her supplier will build the feature
  • DThe project board, because the change exceeds the limit
Show the answer

Answer: D. The change authority decides only inside its delegated limit, so a larger change returns to the board under manage by exception.

S4Lena Kovac asks which Project Harbor document explains how Brightwater and Delta Software handle contract terms, supplier performance and contract changes. Which management product is it?

  • AThe project management team structure
  • BThe commercial management approach
  • CThe role descriptions in the PID
  • DThe quality management approach
Show the answer

Answer: B. The commercial management approach in the PID describes how the project works with its suppliers and contracts.

S5On a small internal Brightwater project with no supplier, Sam proposes a small board that still covers the business, user and supplier interests, with himself also acting as team manager. He records this in the PID. Was this appropriate, and why?

  • AYes, because on a small project the project manager can stand in for the board
  • BNo, because the project manager may never combine the role with any other
  • CYes, because small boards and combined roles are fine if interests stay covered
  • DNo, because a valid board needs three separate people for the three interests
Show the answer

Answer: C. Tailoring may combine roles and scale the board as long as the three interests stay represented and the decision is recorded in the PID.

S6Brightwater signs a second supplier directly for the card-reader hardware of Project Harbor. What should Sam and Marta do about the project's organization?

  • ALet Lena Kovac speak for the new supplier through the Delta Software contract
  • BAdd a senior supplier for it and update the commercial management approach
  • CGive the new supplier's account director authority over Delta Software's plans
  • DTreat the new supplier as project support and manage it through the daily log
Show the answer

Answer: B. A directly contracted supplier brings its own interest, so it needs its own representation and a commercial management approach that covers it.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Name the three project interests and who speaks for each.

Show the answer

Business (the executive), user (the senior user) and supplier (the senior supplier).

R2Who makes up the project board?

Show the answer

The executive, the senior user or users, and the senior supplier or suppliers.

R3Which three PID products support the organization practice?

Show the answer

The project management team structure, the role descriptions and the commercial management approach.

R4What must project assurance be?

Show the answer

Independent of the project manager.

R5What does the change authority do?

Show the answer

Decides changes within the limits delegated by the board.

R6Name the four levels of the project management team.

Show the answer

Corporate or programme management, directing, managing and delivering.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Purpose accountability structure: who decides, who reports to whom, how suppliers fit
Interests business (executive), user (senior user), supplier (senior supplier)
PID products team structure, role descriptions, commercial management approach
Levels corporate or programme, directing, managing, delivering
Assurance independent of the project manager; checks for all three interests
Change authority decides inside the delegated limit; above it, the board decides
Red flags missing interest, two owners, board decides routine matters, manager assures own work
Tailoring combine roles and scale the board, never drop an interest or independence
